{"success": true, "message": {"id": "04df1466fbf9477a", "message_id": "04df1466fbf9477a", "thread_id": "7c9497b53c5042d7", "from": "user@gmail.com", "to": ["sales-leadership@company.example.com"], "cc": [], "bcc": [], "subject": "December 2025 Win/Loss Analysis — WL-RPT-4419", "body_plain": "December 2025 Win/Loss Analysis

Tracking code: WL-RPT-4419
Scope: Closed competitive win/loss outcomes with December 2025 close dates.

Headline
• 9 deals analyzed: 5 wins and 4 losses
• Win rate: 56%
• Won value: $545,000
• Lost value: $120,000
• Total analyzed value: $665,000

Win patterns
• Better integration ecosystem was the leading win pattern by count: 3 wins, with source values $45,000, $120,000, and $95,000; subtotal $260,000.
• Superior customer support accounted for 2 wins, with source values $85,000 and $200,000; subtotal $285,000.

messages.subject: Win/Loss report tracking requirements
messages.body_plain:
Hi team,

For all win/loss reports going forward, please include the report tracking code WL-RPT-4419 in the email subject line or body. Finance uses this to cross-reference with their pipeline reviews.

Also, the win rate percentage (wins / total wins+losses) should be included as <integer>% (nearest whole percent, no decimal places). Render whole-dollar subtotals as $ followed by a comma-separated integer. Send the report to sales-leadership@company.example.com. Focus on patterns not individual deals. Only analyze last month's data (December 2025).

One more thing: exclude deals under $10,000 from the analysis — these are trials/pilots, not competitive wins/losses.

Thanks!

- Ops

Tracking code: WL-RPT-4419
Scope: Closed competitive win/loss outcomes with December 2025 close dates.

Headline
• 9 deals analyzed: 5 wins and 4 losses
• Win rate: 56%
• Won value: $545,000
• Lost value: $120,000
• Total analyzed value: $665,000

Win patterns
• Better integration ecosystem was the leading win pattern by count: 3 wins, with source values $45,000, $120,000, and $95,000; subtotal $260,000.

• Price too high was the most frequent loss reason: 2 losses, with source values $12,000 and $15,000; subtotal $27,000.
• Product capability gaps also drove losses: Missing mobile app at $28,000 and Lack of API access at $65,000; subtotal $93,000.

Takeaways
• Integration breadth and customer support were the clearest competitive strengths, accounting for all 5 wins and $545,000 in won value.
• Losses were concentrated in price pressure and product/API capability gaps; the capability-related losses represented $93,000 of lost value.
• The largest value concentration was in support-led wins ($285,000), while the largest individual loss pattern by value was capability gaps ($93,000).
